Sanjay Vashisth, J. (Oral)
1.

Instant appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants i.e. (1) Manjeet Kaur widow of Ram Singh, along with other claimants (2) Jasbir Kaur (daughter), (3) Kamlajeet Kaur (daughter), (4)
Karamjeet Kaur (minor daughter) and (5) Jitender Singh (minor son), by challenging the award dated 11.03.2005, passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fatehgarh Sahib (for brevity, 'Ld.
Tribunal'), whereby, claim petition i.e. MACT Case No.31/10.10.2002, under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short, 'MV Act'), had been dismissed by the Ld. Tribunal.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fatehgarh Sahib
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
For reference, Section 163-A of the MV Act, is reproduced here-under:-
"163A.

Special provisions as to payment of compensation on structured formula basis.-- (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle of the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in 1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120859 FAO-3910-2005 (O&M) -2- the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation, as Manjeet Kaur And Ors vs Karnail Singh & Ors on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199546662/
1 indicated in the Second Schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

entities.text: Manjeet Kaur And Ors vs Karnail Singh & Ors on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Explanation.--For the purposes of this sub-section, "permanent disability" shall have the same meaning and extent as in the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923).

(2) In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person.
(3) The Central Government may, keeping in view the cost of living by notification in the Official Gazette, from time to time amend the Second Schedule."

3. While deciding issue No.1 i.e. "(1) Whether Ram Singh deceased died in a roadside accident on 18.03.2002, due to rash and negligent driving of Car No. CH-01-H-7959 driven by respondent No.1 ? OPA", Ld. Tribunal observed that FIR (Ex.A1) has been lodged by one Baba Charan Singh, who was the pillion rider.

Said Baba Charan Singh simply stated in FIR that it was Ram Singh, who was driving the Scooter No. PB-10-AG-3126 and he himself was sitting on the backside of his scooter,
which struck against some unidentified thing.
Otherwise also, while dealing with issue No.1, observation was made by Ld. Tribunal in paragraph No.7 and for reference, same is reproduced here-under:-
The onus of this issue is on the claimants.
It is for the claimants to prove that Ram Singh, deceased died on account of 2 of 7 Neutral
Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120859 FAO-3910-2005 (O&M) -3- use of Motor Car No. CH-01-H-7959 driven by respondent no. 1 on 18.03.2002.
To discharge the onus of this issue, the claimants examined AW-1 Manjit Kaur widow of late Ram Singh who was deposed that the husband was 48 years of age at the time of his death.
AW-2 Dheer Singh regarding income of deceased Ram Singh.
The only witness upon which the reliance has been placed by the claimants to prove the death of Ram Singh on account of use of motor car in question.
W-3 is Dilbagh Singh.

He has stated that on 18.03.2002 a green colored car bearing registration No.
CH-01-H-7959 came from the opposite side and hit the scoter of deceased by going on the wrong side.
This witness stated that the driver of the car stopped it at the distance of fifty yards after causing the accident.
That driver of the car was Karnail Singh.
That accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
In cross -examination, he admitted that none of the person then driving the scooter were known to him.
He further stated that he did not know the owner of the scooter on which he was proceeding at that time.
He admitted that ten persons gathered at the spot, but he failed to disclose their names and addresses.
He further stated that pillion rider was semi-conscious.
He further stated that he cannot tell the registration number of the offending van or its occupants.
He further stated that name of the deceased came to his knowledge only on 06.04.2002 as his uncle informed him.
From the perusal of statement of this witness, it has transpired that he failed to tell the number of the scooter on which he was proceeding and the ownership of the same.
He came to know regarding the identity of the deceased on 06.04.2002.

It is Manjeet Kaur And Ors vs Karnail Singh & Ors on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199546662/
2 not believable that the deceased who died on the spot, his identity was not established to the witness if he was present on the spot.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From cross- examination of this witness, his evidence appears shaky.
Undoubtedly PW-4 Inderpreet Singh has stated that challan has been filed against Karnail Singh and charge also has been framed against his vide Ex.A-2 and Ex. A-3.

From close perusal of the evidence on the record, this Tribunal is not prepared to place any 3 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120859 FAO-3910-2005 (O&M) -4- reliance on the statement of AW-3 Dilbagh Singh in this case.
The FIR of this case Ex. A-1 is the most material documents on the record.
The FIR Ex.A-1 hs been lodged by Baba Charan Singh who was the pillion rider.
Baba Charan Singh Singh has simply stated in FIR that Ram Singh was driving the scooter No. PB-10-AG-3126 and he was sitting on the back seat of the scoter struck against some unidentified thing.
That Ram Singh fell down when scooter struck against some unidentified thing.
No number of the vehicle has been given in the FIR nor name of any driver there of has been given in the FIR Ex.Al by the first Informant who was the witness of the accident.
he has nowhere stated that Dilbagh Singh had witnessed this accident.
Baba Charan Singh has also not been examined by claimant who was the natural and best witness in this case.
The name of the Dilbagh Singh AW-3 nowhere figures in FIR.
The FIR neither records the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle nor the name of independent witness Dilbagh Singh.

As such this tribunal has reached the conclusion that it is not safe to place reliance upon the statement of AW3 Dilbagh Singh, more so on account of his cross-examination where he appeared to be a shaky witness.
Baba Charan Singh should have been examined by the claimants on this point as he was the most natural witness in this case.

This tribunal thus places no reliance on the statement AW-3 Dilbagh Singh by relying upon law laid down in Smt. Sarla Devi Vs.
Mool chand and others reported in 2003 (3) The Punjab Law Reporter 169.

entities.text:
Smt. Sarla Devi Vs.
Mool chand and others reported in 2003 (3) The Punjab Law Reporter 169
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mere fact that the challan has been presented against Karnail Singh would not prove this fact because criminal proceeding stand on different footing.

Resultantly, this tribunal has reached the conclusion that claimants have failed to prove that Ram Singh died on account of use of motor car No.
CH-01-H-7959 driven by respondent no. 1 on 18.07.2002.

Issue no., 1 is decided against the claimants accordingly."
4.

From the facts recorded in the reproduced paragraph, this Court 4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120859 FAO-3910-2005 (O&M) -5- also notices that there was one person namely; Karnail Singh, who was found to be driving the car bearing registration No.CH-01-H-7959,
thus, in the happening of accident, involvement and use of the car was also very much established by the Investigating Agency, who conducted its investigation in pursuance to FIR (Ex.A1).
5.

The Insurance Company is not in a position to refute the fact that against the driver of the car namely; Karnail Singh, challan under Section 173 Cr.P.C. was prepared and same was filed before the Court of Illaqa Magistrate, which is available on record of the Tribunal as Ex.A2.

Not only this,
the charges were also framed by the Trial court and said charge-sheet is also available on record as Ex.A3.
6. Taking support of the judgment rendered in Jai Prakash v. M/s National Insurance Company,
2010(2) SCC 607 : Law Finder Doc Id #206127, Mr. Neeraj Khanna, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that it is not within the purview of the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal to proceed further for examining the legality of the investigation process, which in fact,

3 within the domain of the Courts dealing with the criminal cases.

sentences.text: In fact, Tribunals are constituted under the Act, 1988, to conduct the summary proceedings for examining the beneficial provision of law i.e. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, with a prime purpose to rehabilitate the victim's family.

Thus, submits that Ld. Tribunal was expected to see only the prima facie case on the basis of final report under Section 173 Cr.P.C. (Ex.A2), which further got strengthened with the framing of charges by the Court (Ex.A3).
7.

Mr. R.C. Gupta, learned counsel for respondent No.3 -  5 of 7  Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120859 FAO-3910-2005 (O&M) -6- Insurance Company, while defending the observations made by Ld. Tribunal, submits that presence of the witnesses namely; Dilbag Singh and Baba Charan Singh, is highly doubtful at the place of accident.
He also submits that the said Baba Charan Singh has also not been examined and AW3 - Dilbag Singh, nowhere figures in the FIR.
8. Be that as it may, this Court has to examine the evidence of Dilbag Singh (AW3), in its entirety and as an independent piece of evidence.

Moreover, in the circumstances, when there is nothing to dispute that the death of said Ram Singh is because of some other reason than the vehicular accident.
9. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances and the fact recorded in specific that the driver of the Car namely; Karnail Singh was charge-sheeted (Ex.A3) by the trial Court, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the accident occurred due to the involvement of the car bearing registration No.CH-01-H-7959.

However, there being no evidence whereby the said driver was proved to be rash and negligent in his driving and coupled with the fact that the claim petition initially was filed under Section 163-A of the MV Act, I deem appropriate to grant compensation to the appellants/claimants to the tune of Rs.5.00 lakhs, in view of the amended provision i.e. Section 164 of the MV Act (un-amended Section 163-A of the MV Act).

For reaching to the said conclusion, the Court gets strengthen with the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ram Murti and others v. Punjab State Electricity Board, 2023 ACJ 631 : Law Finder Doc id: 2091451 , wherein, the accident had taken place in the year 1994, and compensation amount of Rs.5.00 lakhs, was awarded.

sentences.text: In view of the aforementioned reasons, present appeal is allowed.
Consequently, the impugned order dated 10.01.2004 is hereby set- aside.

Appellants/claimants are held entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.5.00 lakhs, in view of amended provision of law i.e. Section 164 of the MV Act, 1988.
11.
Let the awarded amount of Rs.5.00 lakhs be paid to the appellants/claimants within a period of three months from today by respondent No.3 - Insurance Company.
At this stage, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants urges for granting interest @ 9% per annum, in case of default of payment of compensation amount by respondent No.3 - Insurance Company.
12. I have considered the cited judgments and finds that it is silent about interest part.

However,
considering the date of accident and amended provision of law, it is directed and made clear that in case, the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company does not pay the compensation amount within the stipulated period, as recorded above, in that eventuality, respondent No.3 - Insurance Company would be liable to pay the compensation amount along with interest @ 7.5%
per annum, from the date of passing of this order till its final payment/realization.
Thus by recording aforesaid terms, appeal stands disposed of.
(SANJAY VASHISTH) JUDGE September 11, 2024 J.Ram
